rubrics.justification: It accurately interprets the provided Gardner 1DD grade as a very poor-quality early blastocyst with absent/degenerative ICM and TE, but no image was available and it adds general statements without acknowledging the day-4/grade mismatch or limits on visual assessment.

It integrates age, prior IVF failures/biochemical pregnancies, endometrium, ovarian response, sperm parameters, and lifestyle reasonably well with embryo prognosis, though some links are somewhat speculative.

The reasoning is internally consistent: a 1DD embryo plus age 38 and repeated failed cycles supports a very poor prognosis. Minor issues include overinterpreting sperm as definitively noncontributory and discussing transfer-day implications somewhat inconsistently.

Core interpretation of 1DD as poor prognosis is aligned, but recommendations such as ERA and thrombophilia screening are not routinely guideline-supported for this scenario, and suggesting not transferring is context-dependent rather than standard.

It gives practical next steps for counseling, expectation setting, uterine evaluation, protocol review, and future-cycle options including PGT-A discussion, though some suggestions are broad and not tightly prioritized.
